findings.issue: Source: "it gashed his neck and the blood came pouring from the wound"; candidate: "it grazed his neck, so that blood poured from the wound". "Grazed" softens the wound.
findings.fix: With those words Hector lifted his spear and hurled it. It hit the sevenfold shield on its outermost layer, the eighth, which was bronze. The spear tore through six layers of the shield, but it stuck in the seventh hide. Then Ajax threw. He struck the round shield of the son of Priam, and the terrible spear drove through the gleaming shield and on through the finely worked cuirass. It cut the shirt along Hector’s side, but he swerved, and that saved his life. Each man pulled his spear out of the shield, and they crashed together like savage lions, or like wild boars of great strength and endurance. The son of Priam hit the middle of Ajax’s shield, but the bronze did not break, and the point of his spear bent back. Then Ajax sprang forward and drove his spear through Hector’s shield. It went right through and checked Hector as he lunged to attack, and it gashed his neck, so that blood poured from the wound. Even so Hector kept on fighting. He gave ground and grabbed a huge, rugged stone that lay on the plain with his strong hand. With this he hit the boss in the middle of Ajax’s shield, and the bronze rang out. But Ajax snatched up a far larger stone, swung it high, and hurled it with enormous force. That stone, as big as a millstone, smashed Hector’s shield inward and threw him on his back, with the shield crushing him beneath it. Apollo lifted him up at once. They would then have hacked at each other with their swords in close combat, if the heralds, messengers of gods and men, had not come forward, one from the Trojans and one from the Achaeans. These were Talthybius and Idaeus, both honorable men. They parted the two men with their staves, and the good herald Idaeus said, “My sons, stop fighting. You are both brave men, and both are dear to Zeus. We all know that. But night is falling, and it is good to give way when night commands.”

findings.issue: Butler's "Sit down your own people" is garbled (and "at the hands of hands of Hector" is a typo). Candidate reads sensibly as "Go and sit down among your own people"; "Go and" is an interpretive addition.
